root_cause.text: The goal group index (ac->ac_g_ex.fe_group) can become greater than or equal to the total number of groups (ngroups) due to prior stream allocation, causing the block group search to start at an out-of-bounds group and potentially allocate blocks from groups beyond the 32-bit limit allowed for indirect mapped files.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "If ac->ac_g_ex.fe_group is >= ngroups (for instance, if the goal group was populated via stream allocation from s_mb_last_groups), then start will be >= ngroups. ... its loop uses group = *start, and the very first iteration will call ext4_mb_scan_group() with this unsupported group because next_linear_group() is only called at the end of the iteration." The patch adds the clamp: "if (start >= ngroups) start = 0;"

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard against invalid group index in ext4_mb_scan_groups to avoid out-of-bounds error.
intent_record.what: Added a check to set the starting group index to 0 if it is greater than or equal to the total number of groups.
intent_record.how: If the goal group (fe_group) is invalid (>= ngroups), the scan will start from group 0, preventing out-of-bounds array access.

grouping_result.intent: Guard against invalid group index in ext4_mb_scan_groups to avoid out-of-bounds error.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent is to add a guard against an invalid group index in ext4_mb_scan_groups, which directly addresses the root cause of the vulnerability where the group index can become out of bounds due to prior stream allocation.

candidates.rationale: Directly assigns the goal group index from ac->ac_g_ex.fe_group to start without validation, which can be out-of-bounds due to prior stream allocation.
Uses the potentially invalid start value to set the prefetch group, leading to out-of-bounds access in prefetch logic.
Part of the same initialization block but not directly vulnerable; included for completeness.

vuln_statements.explanation: The goal group index is used directly from ac->ac_g_ex.fe_group without validation, which can be out-of-bounds due to prior stream allocation, leading to a search starting at an invalid group.
Uses the potentially invalid start value to set the prefetch group, causing out-of-bounds access in prefetch logic.
